claims.evidence: No brand markings, casting numbers, or manufacturer tags are visible or reported in either photo; witness only identified it generically as a bare engine assembly.
Cylinder count is not confirmed by the witness; coil/valve cover layout is visible but not counted or described in enough detail to verify configuration.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (compression, bearings, timing issues) invisible from outside photos.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine cranking/running with audible sound, plus a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Missing accessories or components (intake manifold, sensors, ECU, wiring harness ends) reducing usability.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set including intake side and all harness connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: price as incomplete, assume missing parts need sourcing

risks.risk: Mismatch between stated brand/engine code and actual vehicle fitment.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of engine block casting number or ID plate.
risks.if_unproven: price as unconfirmed fitment, buyer bears compatibility risk

risks.risk: Unknown mileage or reason for removal (accident, overheating, fault).
risks.proof: Photo of odometer from donor vehicle or any paperwork/invoice showing removal reason.

risks.risk: No warranty or return policy stated, raising fraud/misrepresentation risk if engine fails after sale.
risks.proof: Written seller statement or screenshot of listing terms on Jiji confirming any warranty.

proof_requests: Video of engine running or at least cranking with sound
Close-up photo of casting/ID number or any brand/model sticker on the block
Photo showing intake manifold side and all wiring harness connectors
Any documentation on vehicle of origin, mileage, or reason for removal
response.reason: The witness confirms this is a bare used engine assembly, so it can be priced at worst case (unverified brand/cylinder count, unknown running condition, possibly incomplete), pending the listed proofs to raise the price.
